newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha easier, near-term spreads seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha easier, near-term spreads seen flat.

text.p: Naphtha prices were a touch lower in dull Tokyo trade, following weaker overseas crude prices on Friday, traders said on Monday.
With both London and New York closed for holidays, activity is expected to remain slow for the rest of the day, they said.
The contango in near-term spreads virtually disappeared, with second-half July/second-half August traded at even.
It changed hands at minus $1.50 last Thursday.
Bids for open-spec naphtha first-half August were heard at $218.00 per tonne, while offers were notionally assessed at $219.00. It stood at $219.00/219.50 on Friday.
Sellers were reluctant to make firm offers amid a lack of market direction from overseas markets today, traders said.
Japan's end-April kerosene stocks ballooned by 50 percent from a year ago due to warmer weather, government data showed.
Middle distillate traders said the stock levels were largely in line with their expectations.

The high inventories are likely to further dampen sentiment in spot kerosene trade, but are unlikely to prompt refiners to cut their crude throughput as some of Japan's major refineries are currently shut for turnarounds, they said.
